findings.summary: Narrowings, 'The grid': 'the host's largest has Z·H = 192 and 128 · 128 programs' joins two different launches' maxima into one sentence.
findings.detail: The largest Z·H (192) is the test's (Z = 4, H = 48, N_CTX = 4096: 32 · 192 = 6144 programs); the largest grid (128 · 128 = 16384 programs) is the benchmark's (Z·H = 128, N_CTX = 16384). Read as written, the sentence describes one launch with both. Suggested wording: 'the host's largest Z·H is 192 (the test) and its largest grid 128 · 128 programs (the benchmark)'. Wording only; the conditions cover both launches.

notes: Checked the model line by line against source lines 248-262 by SEMANTICS.md, with every operator's instance printed with full names (work/Names.lean): all operations are TVA.*, the int32 products and the pointer additions are left to right with the constexprs built in int32, the float16 x float32 product promotes to float32 (BinOp.typing? evaluated), the reduction of a product is tl.sum1c and not tl.sum_bcast_mul. The tolerance's values at HEAD_DIM 16..256 and the README's examples of rejected wrong kernels were re-evaluated exactly (work/tol.py). The conditions cover every launch of the script (test and benchmark); every narrowing is stated with its reason.
